subtitle: Scholars at the Six Gates, Lamps for Distant Mountains

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Vikramashila's central stupa rising over a vast cloister at dusk
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras stand apart in time yet sharing the frame, the king in courtly poise before a plan of monasteries, the monk in travel cloak facing distant snow peaks beyond Vikramashila's great cruciform stupa.

dialogue.text: In the age of the Pālas, Dharmapāla raised brick mahāvihāras, gate-scholars guarded learning, and a monk named Atiśa walked out from Vikramaśīla to change the teachings of Tibet.

i18n.hi: पाल युग में धर्मपाल ने ईंट के महाविहार खड़े किए, द्वार‑पंडितों ने ज्ञान की रखवाली की, और अतिश नाम का भिक्षु विक्रमशिला से निकलकर तिब्बत की शिक्षा बदल गया।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot over the Ganga plains, panning toward Kahalgaon hills
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras appear as small figures in a layered montage over the misty Ganga, with ferries, market boats and distant brick stupas hinting at monasteries rising across the alluvial plains.

dialogue.text: Late in the eighth century, as the Ganga plains filled with guilds, ferries and new shrines, the Pāla king Dharmapāla turned royal power toward brick, monks and manuscripts.

i18n.hi: आठवीं सदी के अंत में, जब गंगा के मैदान संघों, नावों और नए देवालयों से भर रहे थे, पाल राजा धर्मपाल ने राजशक्ति को ईंट, भिक्षुओं और पांडुलिपियों की ओर मोड़ दिया।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in a Pala court, slight low angle on Dharmapala
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras share a symbolic frame: Dharmapala in rich but restrained robes sits on a low throne, counsellors and monks around him, a painted board showing Nalanda, Somapura and Vikramaśīla linked by lines.

dialogue.text: In copperplates and later memories, he is praised as a protector of dharma, endowing great mahāvihāras at Somapura, Vikramaśīla and beyond, weaving a network of monasteries across Bengal and Bihar.

i18n.hi: तांबे की ताम्रपत्रों और बाद की स्मृतियों में वह धर्मरक्षक कहा गया, जिसने सोमपुर, विक्रमशिला और आगे तक विशाल महाविहार बसाए, बंगाल‑बिहार में विहारों का जाल बुन दिया।

panels.shot: bird's-eye view directly over the excavated Vikramashila complex
panels.action: The brick plan of Vikramashila stretches below: a square cloister with neat monk cells, a massive cruciform central shrine and a distinct rectangular building along one edge, all sunlit to reveal their geometry.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, at Kahalgaon, archaeologists uncovered that memory in brick: Vikramaśīla’s vast square court, rows of monk cells, and a cruciform shrine sealed with clay tokens naming the monastery itself.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद कहलगांव में पुरातत्वविदों ने वह याद ईंटों में खोज निकाली: विक्रमशिला का विशाल चौकोर प्रांगण, भिक्षु‑कक्षों की कतारें, और मुद्रांकित मिट्टी से बंद क्रॉसनुमा देवालय जो स्वयं विहार का नाम धारण किए था।

panels.shot: medium shot inside the supposed library building, slight low angle along channels
panels.action: Inside the long rectangular building, rows of low platforms hold stacked palm-leaf bundles, while shallow water channels run beneath, open vents above hinting at cool air flowing through the dim space.

dialogue.text: One hall, with platforms and channels for water-cooled air, is read as a library, where palm-leaf manuscripts were kept dry, cool and safe from the heat of the eastern summer.

i18n.hi: एक सभा‑गृह, जिसमें मंच और ठंडी हवा के लिए जल‑नालियाँ थीं, ग्रंथालय माना गया, जहाँ ताड़पत्र के ग्रंथों को पूरबी गर्मी से सूखा, ठंडा और सुरक्षित रखा जाता था।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Paharpur Somapura mahavihara from ground level
panels.action: The stepped pyramid-like brick core of Somapura at Paharpur rises over a cloister with ruined cells, terracotta plaques still clinging to the walls, under an open sky.

dialogue.text: At Paharpur, the Somapura mahāvihāra shows the same royal ambition: a colossal central shrine, cloisters, cells and ritual paths, its terracotta panels bearing traces of a shared scholastic world.

i18n.hi: पहाड़पुर का सोमपुर महाविहार भी वही शाही चाह दिखाता है: विराट मध्य देवालय, परकोटे, कक्ष और प्रदक्षिणा पथ, जिनकी मृत्तिका पट्टियों पर साझा शास्त्रीय जगत की छाप दिखती है।

panels.shot: medium shot in a Somapura cloister, focus on a young novice
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras appear in layered time: a boy novice in Somapura’s corridor bows to a visiting elder; in the background, ghosted, Dharmapala debates an abbot over a land grant document.

dialogue.text: These mahāvihāras were more than shrines. They held land charters, ran granaries, trained monks in logic and ritual, and linked village fields, city markets and distant courts through learning.

i18n.hi: ये महाविहार केवल देवालय नहीं थे। वे भूमि दान सँभालते, कोठार चलाते, भिक्षुओं को तर्क और अनुष्ठान में साधते, और गाँव के खेतों, नगर बाज़ारों व दूर दरबारों को ज्ञान से जोड़ते थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of Vikramashila's massive gates with scholars seated near each entrance
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras are tiny figures in a dramatic scene: each of Vikramashila’s six great gateways has a seated, composed scholar surrounded by students, scrolls by their side, watching the road.

dialogue.text: Later Tibetan histories remember Vikramaśīla guarded by six gate-scholars, each stationed at a great entrance, testing those who sought to enter with questions in logic, doctrine and debate.

i18n.hi: बाद की तिब्बती कथाएँ कहती हैं कि विक्रमशिला को छह द्वार‑पंडितों ने घेरा था, हर एक महान फाटक पर तैनात, जो भीतर आने वालों को तर्क, सिद्धांत और वाद‑विवाद से परखते थे।

panels.shot: medium close-up on one gate scholar and a nervous visitor, eye-level
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras share the frame symbolically: a grave gate scholar lifts his hand mid-question to a travelling monk, whose lips form a careful reply, while in a faded overlay Atisha listens nearby as a young student.

dialogue.text: The Blue Annals names over a hundred learned teachers there. In its telling, only those who answered well could pass the gates, keeping idle talk and shallow teaching outside.

i18n.hi: ब्लू एनल्स में वहाँ के सौ से अधिक आचार्यों के नाम हैं। उसकी कथा में, केवल वही द्वार पार कर पाते जो उत्तर में खरे उतरते, यूँ फालतू गप और ऊपरी सतही ज्ञान बाहर ही रहता।

panels.shot: medium shot in a Vikramashila classroom, slightly high angle
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras appear as teacher and pupil: Atiśa, robed simply, sits cross-legged among other monks while a senior masters the chalked diagram of syllogisms on a ground board.

dialogue.text: Into this world, in the early eleventh century, came Atiśa from Vikrampur in eastern Bengal, moving through the Pāla network from vihāra to vihāra, steeped in debate, ritual and meditation.

i18n.hi: इसी जगत में, ग्यारहवीं सदी की शुरुआत में, पूरबी बंगाल के विक्रमपुर से अतिशा आया, पाल विहारों की कड़ी पर विहार से विहार चलता, वाद, कर्मकांड और ध्यान में डूबा हुआ।

panels.shot: close-up on Atisha in contemplation in the cooled library, three-quarter profile
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras overlap in time: Atiśa sits in the dim library, fingers resting on a palm-leaf manuscript, eyes calm as a shaft of cooler air touches fluttering hanging cloths above the water channels.

dialogue.text: In such cooled halls he studied Prajñāpāramitā and Vinaya. Later accounts remember him also journeying to Suvarnadvīpa for further training, carrying Vikramaśīla’s discipline into wider seas of learning.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं ठंडी सभाओं में उसने प्रज्ञापारमिता और विनय पढ़ा। बाद के वृत्तांत उसे सुवर्णद्वीप तक और साधना के लिए जाते याद करते हैं, विक्रमशिला की कठोरता को व्यापक समुद्रों तक ले जाते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of a debating courtyard with monks in two rows, low side angle
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras stand among rows of seated monks in a debate court, one side speaking in turn while the other listens; a gate scholar watches from behind a pillar, gauging the sharpness of arguments.

dialogue.text: Within the cloister, debates echoed under the brick arches. Vinaya against laxity, Madhyamaka against misconception, reason against habit—each victory meant another lamp kept clear of smoke.

i18n.hi: परकोटे के भीतर, ईंट की मेहराबों के नीचे वाद‑विवाद गूँजते। विनय ढील के विरुद्ध, मध्यमक भ्रांति के विरुद्ध, विचार आदत के विरुद्ध—हर जीत का मतलब एक दीया और धुएँ से बचा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Atisha receiving envoys from Tibet, interior hall, frontal
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras inhabit a solemn scene: Tibetan envoys in heavy cloaks bow before Atiśa in a Vikramashila hall, their leader offering gifts and a letter, while fellow monks watch in mingled curiosity and concern.

dialogue.speaker: dharmapala_and_atisha
dialogue.text: Our land pleads for clear teaching, master. Will you come?

i18n.hi: “गुरुदेव, हमारी भूमि साफ ज्ञान की गुहार लगाती है। क्या आप चलेंगे?”

panels.shot: close-up on Atisha's face, thoughtful, slight low angle
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras are framed as Atiśa, eyes lowered, weighs the request, the shadow of Vikramashila’s stupa falling across his shoulder as if the whole institution leans in on his choice.

dialogue.text: The Blue Annals says he hesitated. Tibet already had centuries of Buddhism; yet its patrons sought reform, a fresh ordering of vows and practice from a master of Vikramaśīla.

i18n.hi: ब्लू एनल्स कहता है, वह ठिठका। तिब्बत में पहले से सदियों का बौद्ध धर्म था; पर वहाँ के संरक्षक सुधार चाहते थे—विक्रमशिला के आचार्य से नए सिरे से व्रत और साधना की व्यवस्था।

panels.shot: medium shot in a council of monks at Vikramashila, eye-level
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras sit among elder monks in council; some gesture toward the distant Himalaya on a painted cloth map, others toward the shelves of manuscripts behind them, a quiet tension in their hands.

dialogue.text: Council was held. To send a leading scholar was to lose a pillar at home, yet it showed the reach of Pāla mahāvihāras. Atiśa agreed, on condition that monastic discipline be kept firm.

i18n.hi: सभा हुई। किसी अग्रणी पंडित को भेजना घर की एक स्तंभ खोना था, पर इससे पाल महाविहारों की पहुँच भी दिखती थी। अतिशा ने सहमति दी, शर्त पर कि मठ‑अनुशासन सख्त रखा जाए।

panels.shot: wide shot of Atisha departing by boat on the Ganga, three-quarter rear
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras are separated by time: Atiśa stands on a riverboat leaving the Ganga bank near Vikramashila, looking back at the brick silhouette; in the far sky, Dharmapala appears faintly, watching his institution’s light travel.

dialogue.text: So a monk raised in Vikrampur and trained at Vikramaśīla stepped onto the river, carrying with him not a new faith for Tibet, but a particular balance of ethics, meditation and wisdom forged in the Pāla cloisters.

i18n.hi: तो विक्रमपुर में पला और विक्रमशिला में तपा भिक्षु नाव पर चढ़ा, तिब्बत के लिए कोई नया धर्म नहीं, बल्कि पाल विहारों में गढ़ी नीति, ध्यान और प्रज्ञा का खास संतुलन लेकर।

panels.shot: medium shot in Tibet, Atisha teaching to a small assembly, slight low angle
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras appear as Atiśa now sits in a Tibetan hall, snow mountains glimpsed through a window, explaining a structured path text to monks in heavy robes, a palm-leaf manuscript from Bengal open before him.

dialogue.text: In Tibet he composed and taught a graded path, later central to Tibetan tradition. Through him, the disciplines and cautions of Vikramaśīla entered Himalayan lineages and were remembered long after Pāla power faded.

i18n.hi: तिब्बत में उसने क्रमबद्ध मार्ग रचा और पढ़ाया, जो बाद में तिब्बती परंपरा का मेरुदंड बना। उसके जरिये विक्रमशिला की सावधानियाँ और अनुशासन हिमालयी वंशों में उतरे और पालों के ढलने के बाद भी याद रहे।

panels.shot: wide shot of ruined Vikramashila in twilight, slow push-in
panels.action: The ruined walls of Vikramashila stand in soft twilight, grass growing over brick, the central cruciform mound rising in silhouette; no people are present, only birds wheeling above.

dialogue.text: Later centuries brought neglect and, in time, ruin. The brick cloisters fell silent, their water channels dry, their gate-scholars remembered only in distant chronicles and the broken seals unearthed from the earth.

i18n.hi: आगे की सदियाँ उपेक्षा, फिर विनाश लेकर आईं। ईंट के परकोटे खामोश हो गए, उनकी जल‑नालियाँ सूख गईं, द्वार‑पंडित बस दूर की कथाओं और मिट्टी से निकले टूटी मुहरों में बचे।

panels.shot: high-angle composite shot linking ruins, manuscripts, and distant mountains
panels.action: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras appear as translucent figures over a triptych: the excavated plan of Vikramashila, a close view of a palm-leaf manuscript, and snow peaks where monks chant from Atiśa’s texts.

dialogue.text: Dharmapāla’s mahāvihāras did not outlast all storms, yet their design, discipline and scholars shaped minds far beyond their bricks—showing how institutions endure when they train others to carry away the light.

i18n.hi: धर्मपाल के महाविहार हर आँधी से नहीं बचे, पर उनकी रचना, अनुशासन और पंडित ईंटों से बहुत दूर तक मन गढ़ते रहे—दिखाते हुए कि संस्थान तब तक टिकते हैं, जब तक वे दूसरों को रोशनी लेकर चलना सिखाते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: Scholars at the Six Gates, Lamps for Distant Mountains
subtitle_i18n.hi: छह द्वारों के पंडित, दूर पहाड़ों के दीये
